_comment: Manifest of the checked skill examples. `check-skill-examples.sh` and
`check-skill-example-ts.sh` are driven from this file rather than from
hardcoded paths, so adding a route means adding an entry here.
THE RULE THAT EARNS THE MANIFEST: every binding in `bindings` must appear
in either `files` or `absent` for every route. A binding named in neither
is an error, not a skip. Otherwise a route that quietly covers three
languages reads exactly like one that covers five.
`absent` is for a binding that will not get this example, with the reason.
It is not a to-do list — a route that is merely unwritten yet should say
`run` holds the execution contract: the stdout regex the example must match
and the timeout. A compile floor cannot catch an example that builds and then
hangs — which is exactly what hello.* did — so anything listed here is also
executed. `run.not_wired` names bindings whose artifacts are not available in
the job that runs the others, with the reason; same rule as `absent`, so a
partially-executed route can never read as a fully-executed one.

examples.title: Hello, mesh
examples.route: construct · publish · verify the bus accepted it · shutdown

not_wired.python: needs the maturin-built binding; not executed anywhere yet — ci.yml's sdk-py-tests is where it belongs
not_wired.go: cgo — needs the libnet cdylib; not executed anywhere yet — ci.yml's go-tests is where it belongs
not_wired.c: needs libnet built and linked; not executed anywhere yet — ci.yml's ffi-tests is where it belongs
